Summary
Jack Beckerman, an enlisted soldier, is writing to someone about his desire to be released from service by December 1st. He mentions that if approved, he will undergo some administrative processing and then wait for a ship to leave. He also discusses the improvement in morale and shipping conditions, and expresses hope for good news from Abe. He reassures the recipient that he will keep them informed and to be patient.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_93a) --- Dear Folks: Nothing new during the past week. Have gotten to work on trying to get out as soon as possible. Took the first step by writing to my commanding officer stating that I would like to be made available for separation as of 1 December. If that is approved than things should go pretty easy after that. altho enlisted --- Page 2 (Beckerman_93b) --- men have to be released as soon as they become eligible; officers may be held for 60 days if they are considered "essential". As soon as my request is approved my name will be submitted to Hdg's for some paper processing and then all I have to do is wait for a boat. By the way we've had excellent news during the last two weeks of shipping --- Page 3 (Beckerman_93c) --- 3 space because available and almost all returners were cleared out of the shipping depots. Morale took a sharp climb when that happened. Also have read where the War Dept. has allocated a large number of ships for our use. Haven't received any thing from Abe - am hoping that you've heard some good news from him. I'll shall keep you in touch --- Page 4 (Beckerman_93d) --- There will be NO surprises. I'll let you have all the news - good or bad. I will send you a cablegram before I leave. So don't get scared if the Telegraph says [illegible] you. and let's try to be a little patient thru the last [illegible]. Keep well. Love Jack
